overall_diagnosis: All samples converge on a single localized issue: Workflow 2 in senior-data-engineer/SKILL.md gives incorrect/ambiguous guidance for this Flink sessionization/query task about (1) how to determine “job finished/completion” and (2) which jobs qualify to emit final output. The guidance likely conflates stage/session closure (10-minute SUBMIT inactivity gap in event time) with job completion, or permits emitting results too early / for non-completed jobs, leading to missing/extra outputs and incorrect longest-stage computation. Other skill files are not implicated.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Workflow 2 has flawed or underspecified rules for completion-event determination and output eligibility in streaming/session-style problems: it likely (a) infers job completion from inactivity/session closure, or (b) relies on an explicit terminal event when the task requires inactivity-gap logic for stages, and/or (c) allows emitting intermediate/incomplete aggregates or emitting for all keys seen instead of only eligible completed jobs.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction:
Revise Workflow 2 to clearly separate and precisely define: (1) stage/session boundaries vs (2) job completion vs (3) output emission.
- Stage/sessionization: define stages purely by task SUBMIT events using an event-time inactivity gap of 10 minutes (i.e., submissions <10 minutes apart are same stage; >=10 minutes starts new stage), with correct handling of event-time, watermarks, and allowed lateness (if relevant).
- Resubmissions: explicitly state repeated SUBMITs (including after fail/evict/reschedule) are counted as distinct SUBMIT events and participate in stage grouping per the gap rule.
- Job completion gating: define “job finished” strictly via job-level terminal state/events when present (joined by jobId), not inferred from task inactivity; if terminal job events are absent, specify an explicit fallback (e.g., end-of-input/watermark-based closure) and document it.
- Output eligibility: state that final results are emitted once per job only after that job satisfies the completion rule; avoid broad rules like “emit for all jobs/keys observed” or “emit on any terminal event regardless of event-time ordering,” and avoid emitting partial/intermediate stage aggregates unless the task explicitly asks for them.
